key_headlines.title: Deputy PM Koo Expands FTA Strategy to Emerging Markets Amid US Trade Pressures
key_headlines.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Koo Yoon-chul announced plans to expand free trade agreements to emerging markets in Southeast Asia, Latin America, and Africa to diversify global supply chains while responding strategically to US Section 301 trade investigations.

key_headlines.title: US Section 301 Investigation Poses Differentiated Risks to Korean Exports by Sector
key_headlines.summary: Semiconductors and shipbuilding sectors face minimal tariff threats under US Section 301 investigations as US demand remains strong, while steel and other structurally overproductive industries face higher tariff risks with responses due April 15th.

key_headlines.title: Stagflation Fears Mount as Oil Prices Surge and Growth Projections Decline
key_headlines.summary: Oil prices jumped 9% to over 105 dollars amid Middle East tensions while Korea's 2026 growth forecast fell to 1% from earlier projections of 2%, raising stagflation concerns for emerging Asian economies.

key_headlines.title: Bank of Korea Governor Candidate Projects Supplementary Budget to Boost Growth by 0.2%
key_headlines.summary: BOK Governor nominee Shin Hyun-song stated that supplementary budget spending will increase growth by 0.2 percentage points while maintaining limited impact on inflation and exchange rates through targeted support.

key_headlines.title: Jeonse Rental Market Collapses with Monthly Rents Rising to 3 Million Won as Government Tightens Lending Regulations
key_headlines.summary: Seoul jeonse transactions plummeted 34% year-over-year as government regulatory tightening accelerates conversion to monthly rentals, with even single-homeowner jeonse lending now facing restrictions previously considered off-limits.

sections.Hot Economy News: Deputy Prime Minister Koo Yoon-chul announced comprehensive strategies to counter protectionist trade pressures and geopolitical risks, emphasizing expansion of free trade agreements to emerging markets in Southeast Asia, Latin America, and Africa. The government is preparing responses to US Section 301 trade investigations due April 15th, asserting that Korean manufacturing capacity utilization remains appropriate and defending against overproduction accusations. Additionally, the administration plans to strengthen development finance mechanisms beyond traditional ODA to support supply chain diversification. These measures represent Korea's dual approach of expanding trade relationships while addressing immediate US tariff threats through diplomatic engagement.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: Stagflation concerns are intensifying as crude oil prices surged 9% to over 105 dollars amid escalating Middle East tensions, while Korea's 2026 growth forecast has declined sharply to around 1%, well below the Bank of Korea's 2.0% projection and OECD's 1.7% estimate. Bank of Korea Governor nominee Shin Hyun-song projected that the supplementary budget would increase growth by 0.2 percentage points while maintaining limited impact on inflation and currency movements through targeted support to vulnerable households and exporters. The divergence between rising commodity prices and weakening growth creates stagflationary pressures, particularly affecting emerging Asian economies like Korea. Inflation concerns are mounting with projections suggesting Korea's consumer price increases could reach 4.2% this year, while real economic growth remains weak.
sections.Financial Markets: Financial markets experienced significant volatility driven by Middle East tensions and US monetary policy uncertainty, with the KOSPI declining 0.86% and the Korean won approaching 1,500 to the dollar as oil prices spiked. US Treasury yields rose sharply, with the 10-year yield reaching 4.339%, reflecting inflation concerns and risk-off sentiment spreading to Korean bond markets. Volatility indices for KOSPI and KOSDAQ surged to 2.5 times monthly averages following Middle East escalations, while individual retail investors shifted capital from large-cap KOSPI stocks to growth-focused KOSDAQ stocks. Currency and bond market pressures intensified as international funds remain cautious amid geopolitical uncertainties and divergent central bank policies.
sections.Industry & Technology: The semiconductor and shipbuilding sectors are positioned to weather US Section 301 trade investigations relatively unscathed due to strong US demand for these products, while steel and other industries facing structural overproduction charges face elevated tariff risks. Battery and steel manufacturers facing weakened business conditions view AI transformation as essential to survival, with industry leaders expressing concerns about competing in increasingly imbalanced market conditions. Both semiconductors and automobiles remain critical pillars supporting the Korean economy, but labor unions' planned spring strikes in these sectors pose additional risks to production stability. Industry experts emphasize the need for AI-driven productivity improvements and competitive differentiation strategies to counter protectionist trade pressures.
sections.Real Estate: Seoul's jeonse rental market experienced a dramatic 34% decline in transactions year-over-year as accelerating monthly rent conversions reshape the rental landscape, with monthly rents for standard residential units now reaching 3 million won levels. Government authorities expanded lending regulations to restrict even single-homeowner jeonse loans, a threshold previous administrations avoided, signaling intensified efforts to suppress real estate speculation and volatility. The Bank of Korea reports that monthly rent proportions in apartment lease contracts more than doubled from 2.4% in August 2021 to 5.5% in August 2025, directly attributable to government lending restrictions and shrinking jeonse supply. Financial constraints from tightened lending policies are accelerating landlords' conversions to monthly rentals, fundamentally restructuring the rental market and affecting housing affordability for lower-income households.
sections.International Economy: Middle East tensions centered on the Hormuz Strait escalated dramatically with the US implementing counter-blockade measures while Iran denounced American actions as illegal piracy, raising crude oil prices and creating global energy supply uncertainties. Trump administration signals suggest potential negotiations with Iran may be possible, temporarily supporting a modest recovery in US equity markets and reducing some currency volatility, though comprehensive resolution remains uncertain. China called for immediate ceasefires warning that blockades threaten global trade, while major European allies maintained diplomatic silence regarding US counter-blockade actions. Japan's central bank is considering rate increases amid rising energy-driven inflation, with market expectations placing the probability of April rate hikes at approximately 60%, affecting broader Asian monetary policy dynamics.
sections.AI & Economy: Seoul is investing 18.8 billion won in AI and space industry research and development through the Seoul-type R&D support program, which has cumulatively supported over 4,550 projects totaling 8.1 billion won since 2005. Hyundai Motor announced 26 billion dollar investments in the US focused on robotics and physical AI development, positioning the company to capitalize on emerging automation trends while adapting to protectionist trade environments. Government and labor experts participating in parliamentary discussions on AI transformation recognize that AI will reconfigure rather than eliminate jobs, emphasizing the need for workforce retraining programs and expanded social safety nets to address labor market polarization risks. Major construction companies like Daewoo E&C are establishing dedicated task forces for data center development to capitalize on AI infrastructure demand growth, signaling broad-based recognition of AI as critical economic infrastructure.
sections.Others: The government and Democratic Party are jointly pursuing auto insurance rate reductions for vehicles participating in 2-part and 5-part operating restrictions to offset higher transportation costs from Middle East energy disruptions, with rate cuts expected to be announced within the following week. Student loan delinquency reached record levels at 80 billion won as youth employment instability and rising living costs deteriorated repayment conditions, prompting National Assembly Budget Office recommendations to increase income thresholds for loan repayment obligations. Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency issued practical implementation guidelines for the EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism ahead of 2028 expanded application to 180 product categories, requiring Korean exporters to secure carbon certifications. Iran condemned US maritime blockade measures as piracy while vowing strong retaliation against Hormuz Strait restrictions, intensifying geopolitical uncertainties affecting global energy and trade flows.
